transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we finalize the remote instruction plan for tomorrow, I need to raise an important family access concern. My team completed family outreach confirmations this week, and we've identified 38 households that lack reliable internet access. The current draft plan assumes families can use digital materials, but these households will need printed learning packets and bilingual phone check-ins in Spanish and Somali. This information isn't reflected in the draft yet because the family-access summary is still being compiled. I'd like to make sure we address this before Dr. Lee signs off on the plan.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: I need to share a critical transportation finding before we finalize this plan. My department completed our storm route review this afternoon, and the results show that no buses can safely travel tomorrow. This means we cannot send meals by regular bus routes as the current draft plan assumes. Instead, meals can be made available for on-site pickup at North Campus and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. These route review results have not yet been added to the operations briefing packet, so Dr. Lee would not have this information when reviewing the plan.

Ms. Shah, if no buses can safely travel tomorrow, then the draft plan's meal delivery by regular bus routes is not viable, and we'll need to revise that to your on-site pickup alternative at North Campus and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Ms. Green, the 38 households without reliable internet access also need to be addressed — the plan can't assume universal digital access. We should incorporate printed learning packets and bilingual phone check-ins in Spanish and Somali for those families. I also want to flag that the draft currently directs health questions to the usual school voicemail — I'd like to hear from nursing on whether that approach is adequate for a remote day. Let's get the updated plan drafted with these revisions incorporated.

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, to answer your question about whether directing health questions to the usual school voicemail is adequate for a remote day — it is not sufficient. Our district nurse coverage plan requires a staffed nurse hotline from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. tomorrow for students who need medication or urgent health guidance during remote instruction. I confirmed the coverage roster this afternoon, but it has not yet been entered in the plan. We need to replace the voicemail direction with the staffed hotline information before the plan is finalized.

transcript.text: I need to share a critical IT finding before we finalize this plan. District learning-management-system authentication will be offline for scheduled maintenance from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m. tomorrow. I confirmed this maintenance window with the vendor today, but the vendor notice has not yet been attached to the remote-day draft. This means the draft plan's assumption that instruction begins through the LMS at 8:00 a.m. is not viable. Instead, instructional files must be distributed by email as downloadable PDFs and made available for printing by 7:30 a.m. This also intersects with Ms. Green's concern — the 38 households without internet access will need those printed packets ready by 7:30 a.m. as well.
